title: Browser-playable 3D kung fu hack-and-slash in about a week
author: dbdbdeep
selftext:
A 10-minute 3D kung fu hack-and-slash that runs in the browser: a guy from the future in a jacket and jeans fights his way up a mountain fortress – crowds, parries, executions, full-screen ultimate cinematics, a floating boss. Free on itch, best on PC, phones work in landscape.



Play: [https://echoplayroom.itch.io/murims-last-hope](https://echoplayroom.itch.io/murims-last-hope)

  


\*\*How it was made\*\*



\- \*\*Code:\*\* I directed, Claude Code wrote it – about 40,000 lines of JavaScript on three.js. Big feature batches ran as several agents in parallel, each in its own git worktree, then got merged and checked by separate verify agents (browser smoke tests, performance budgets, 850 automated tests).

\- \*\*3D:\*\* enemies and the boss are AI-generated models from Meshy; animations come from a CC0 library plus Meshy clips, retargeted onto the hero by agent-written scripts. Most effects are procedural shaders.

\- \*\*Audio:\*\* 148 sound effects generated through the ElevenLabs sound effects API (prompted, trimmed and loudness-matched by an agent), music generated with ElevenLabs.

\- \*\*English version:\*\* a glossary pass by three "translator" agents (genre-faithful, comedy, UI length limits) merged into one, then about 500 UI strings moved into dictionaries.

\- \*\*Trailer:\*\* an agent built a capture tool that steps the game clock frame by frame, so the trailer is a clean 60fps capture of the real game, cut to the music.



\*\*My part:\*\* design, direction and a lot of playtesting. Every round of "this feels wrong" turned into the next batch of agent tasks.



\*\*Things only playtesting caught\*\*



\- The music played the whole time – at volume zero.

\- Every hit flashed enemies into flat white silhouettes, frozen by hit-stop. Hits now scale blood, sparks and bone dust with damage.

\- The final boss needed up to four executions because her numbers were tuned for a weaker enemy.

\- Guards on the first two areas just stood and stared.

\- On itch, the keyboard did nothing until you clicked the game (iframe focus).



Happy to answer questions about the workflow. Feedback on the game itself is very welcome too.
